description: Execution routing policy: facet classification, evidence discipline, obligations, rerouting.

triggers: No shared contract or runtime semantics changed
obligations: Overflow and accessible-name checks if affected

triggers: Selection, focus, validation, derived totals, URL state, form state
obligations: Pure-logic assertions for computed values and state transitions
facets.invariant: For computed properties, record inputs and invariant, not merely the formula. Test with independently specified examples - never copy the production selector into the oracle.

triggers: External API calls, retries, polling, real-time subscriptions
Global tokens, shared component, shared schema
Dependency lockfile, design system changes, shared utility
obligations: Broad fallback when mapping is incomplete
facets.invariant: Use union of base and head graphs so deleted/moved nodes stay visible in impact analysis.

obligations: Denial cases (unauthorized access must be rejected)
facets.invariant: Gateway auth does not prove object-level auth. Browser-hidden controls do not enforce permissions. Caches must not bypass tenant scope.

triggers: Missing mapping (changed file has no known contract)
obligations: Repository fallback suite if subsystem cannot be established

facet_rules.rationale: An auth change that also changes an API shape needs both sets of checks.

evidence_status.rule: Agent statements without supporting evidence (test output, grep, git diff, traces) remain hypotheses. Boolean false, unknown, and not-applicable are different states.

obligation_lifecycle.removal_rule: Remove only with recorded evidence that the obligation's premise is false.
obligation_lifecycle.gap_rule: Mandatory obligation with no executable check prevents verified status.

outcomes.action: Repair implementation; rerun failed + affected checks
Diagnose environment; preserve implementation; report blocked
Correct test with contract reference; rerun relevant checks
Produce contract decision with options and consequences
Add facet/obligations; recompute impact; retain task goal

outcomes.condition: Same failure persists without new evidence
outcomes.action: Leave patch loop for diagnosis; stop speculative edits
Capture deduplicated issue candidate; continue unless blocked

loop_budget.evidence_producing_rule: A repair is evidence-producing only if it changes implementation in response to a specific hypothesis informed by failure output. A blind retry is not evidence-producing.
loop_budget.exhaustion_result: Reproducible blocked handoff, not success or automatic abandonment.
loop_budget.flaky_rule: A test becoming green only after retry remains instability to investigate, not clean verification.

criteria: All changes mapped to known contracts
Known ownership for all affected nodes
No touched trust, persistence, or shared boundary
No unmapped or unresolved dynamic edges
fast_path.rule: All must be affirmatively true. A one-line patch can still be high risk.

priority_routing.default: Preserve current work. Switch only for incident, explicit reprioritization, or genuine blocker.

principles.principle: All loops must have a fixed, provable upper bound.
Check every return value. Unchecked returns are unchecked obligations.

principles.source: AWS formal methods (Newcombe et al., CACM 2015)
principles.principle: Specify invariants for high-risk components, not everything. The facet classification identifies what needs deeper analysis; the fast path lets simple changes through.
Hermetic = deterministic. Tests touching shared state are flaky candidates.

exemplars.pattern: Convention enforcement: every registered route introspected at test time to verify auth decorator present. 3 named exceptions, pinned in both directions.
exemplars.why: Auth coverage enforced by test, not discipline. Renamed routes fail. Stale exemptions fail.

exemplars.pattern: Boot-time guards refuse to start with unsafe configuration: disabled auth on hosted sites, weak JWT secrets, missing passwords.
exemplars.why: Security posture is fail-closed. Defaults are the safe answer.

exemplars.pattern: Write response envelope declares which GET paths a write invalidated. Test asserts every template matches a live registered route.
exemplars.why: Cache invalidation contract is machine-readable and tested. Renamed routes are test failures, not stale 404s.

exemplars.pattern: Stateless HTTP replaces modal UI dialogs. 409 response includes retry payload. Unknown keys refused. bool('false') pitfall addressed.
exemplars.why: Dangerous-direction validation: the one boolean interpretation that silently does the wrong thing is explicitly tested.
